rows.text: Liu started his career teaching at a technical school; in 1982 he and his three brothers quit government jobs to invest in breeding quails and chickens for sale to Sichuan farmers.
In 1992, Liu and his brothers moved into the animal feed business and founded Hope Group, which by 2010 had become the largest animal-feed group in China.
Liu helped establish China Minsheng Bank, becoming vice-chairman and by 1999 its largest shareholder; by 2011 he held about 7 percent of the bank's shares.
Quit a government job in 1982 alongside three brothers to start a quail- and chicken-breeding business in Sichuan.
New Hope Group grew into China's largest animal-feed producer by 2010, per Wikipedia, and Liu was named one of Fortune's 15 business people who changed China in 2012.
Liu Chang became chairman of New Hope Liuhe in 2013, marking a generational leadership transition at the listed subsidiary.

Lu was born into a peasant family, dropped out of school at 15, and worked as an ironsmith before co-founding a small factory with six other farmers in July 1969 to produce small agricultural machines.

Lu grew the original agricultural-machinery workshop into Wanxiang Group, a large manufacturing conglomerate and leading producer of automobile components, while also serving as a part-time EMBA professor at Zhejiang University.
33 on the Forbes China Rich List with an estimated 13.13 billion yuan (about $1.87 billion) -- and was reported as the richest person in Zhejiang Province.
Co-founded a small agricultural-machinery factory with six other farmers in Xiaoshan, Hangzhou in July 1969.
Took over as director of Great Wall Motor in 1990 and led the company through privatization in 1998 and a Hong Kong Stock Exchange listing in 2003.
GWM became one of the top ten Chinese automobile manufacturers, publicly listed and privatized under Wei's leadership.
Diversified GWM into multiple vehicle brands and formed a 2019 joint venture with BMW Group to produce electric Mini vehicles in China.

GWM sold 1.23 million vehicles globally in 2024 and 1,323,672 vehicles in 2025 across its multi-brand portfolio, with the BMW joint venture (Spotlight Automotive) operating as part of its electrification push.
Founded Bluestar in 1984 as a small industrial-solvents factory and grew it into China National Bluestar Group.
From 1996, consolidated more than 100 troubled, government-owned chemical factories into what became ChemChina, later pursuing the acquisition of Syngenta.
ChemChina grew into the Fortune Global 500's 265th-largest company and completed the roughly $43 billion Syngenta acquisition, with Ren also becoming chairman of Pirelli.
Ma's first job was at China Motion Telecom Development, where he developed pager software for a reported $176 per month, before co-founding Tencent in 1998 with four university classmates.
Co-founded Tencent in 1998 with four classmates and led the company's development of the OICQ/QQ messaging product in 1999.

Jindal held elected office in Haryana and served as a state power minister, an unusually direct combination of industrial and political authority that is treated as emblematic of the licence-era promoter-house posture toward the state.

The direct political role is often read as both an enabler — for licensing and policy access — and a complicator, exposing the group to the political cycle in ways that purely commercial houses were not.
Cao was born in 1946 in Fuqing, Fujian, into a family that had been wealthy but lost everything fleeing the Chinese civil war, forcing him to leave school at age 14 to help support the family.

Cao built Fuyao Group into one of the world's largest glass manufacturers, with the company specializing in automotive glass, and holds leadership roles in industry bodies including the China Automobile Glass Association.
Cao serves as a member of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference representing Fujian, connecting his business role to a formal advisory political body.
Fuyao Group became one of the largest glass manufacturers globally, per Wikipedia's characterization, with Cao continuing as chairman.
Liu's father, a comprador at a major Chinese shipping firm, died when Liu was six, leaving the family in financial difficulty; Liu attended St.
John's University in Shanghai on scholarship and built a business network there before entering commerce.

Liu diversified aggressively across unrelated industries -- matches, cement, coal, and wool textiles -- rather than concentrating on a single sector, earning him the nicknames "Match King" and "Wool King".
Built a diversified industrial conglomerate beginning with match manufacturing, then expanding into cement, coal, and wool textiles.
Liu became one of Republican Shanghai's most prominent industrialists, with holdings across multiple sectors, per Wikipedia and Global Times profiles.
Remained on the mainland after 1949 and cooperated with the new Communist government rather than relocating his business interests abroad.
Liu was granted protected 'nationalist capitalist' status by the CCP and served in national political bodies (NPC delegate, CPPCC member) until his death in 1956.
Liu founded JD.com in 2004 and received China's 'Person of the Year of Chinese Economy 2011' award from CCTV, and was named among Fortune's 'World's 50 Greatest Leaders' in 2015.
Stepped down as CEO in April 2022, handing the role to company president Xu Lei while remaining chairman.

Liu retained the chairman role and continued serving as chairman of related entities including Jingdong Technology Holding (since June 2020), JD Health International (since September 2020), and JD Logistics.
Founded Nine Dragons Paper Holdings, building a recycled-paper and cardboard manufacturing business tied to US scrap-paper imports.
Nine Dragons Paper grew into China's biggest paper maker, and Zhang became one of the richest women in greater China, earning the nickname 'Queen of Trash' per Wikipedia.

Liang attended Zhejiang University, earning both bachelor's and master's degrees in engineering, and began his career applying machine-learning methods to quantitative finance before co-founding High-Flyer.
Through High-Flyer, Liang built large-scale computing infrastructure originally for quantitative finance that was later repurposed to support AI research, leading to DeepSeek's founding in July 2023.

Before Meituan, Wang built and lost control of a Facebook clone called Xiaonei (later rebranded Renren after being sold due to financial problems) and founded microblogging site Fanfou in 2007, which was shut down by the government.

Wang holds a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering from Tsinghua University and pursued but did not complete a PhD in computer engineering at the University of Delaware, leaving with a master's degree instead.
Founded and grew Muyuan Foods into the world's largest pig-farming and breeding operation over more than two decades.
Muyuan Foods' revenue nearly doubled from RMB 78.89 billion (2021) to RMB 144.15 billion (2025), and the company became the global leader in pig farming and breeding by volume.
Resigned as chairman, director, and president on June 3, 2026, transitioning to a Lifetime Honorary Chairman and research-institute role, with Cao Zhinian taking over as chairman.
The leadership transition was completed as of the June 3, 2026 announcement, with Cao Zhinian installed as chairman and Qin retaining an honorary and research-focused role.

On May 19, 2026, following shareholder approval at Nongfu Spring's annual general meeting, Zhong Shanshan was appointed chairman of the company's newly elected Ninth Board of Directors, a term set to run three years from that date.
Was re-elected/re-appointed as chairman of Nongfu Spring's Ninth Board of Directors, effective May 19, 2026, for a three-year term.
Zhong's chairmanship was formally renewed through the Ninth Board's three-year term beginning May 19, 2026.

Zhang Jian placed first in the highest imperial civil-service examination in 1894, then abandoned officialdom in 1895 to found the Dasheng Cotton Mill in his home region of Nantong, choosing industry over a conventional mandarin career.

Zhang framed his industrial and educational projects around building a modern domestic economy that could resist foreign commercial and political pressure on China, later founding schools, a museum, and a planetarium alongside his mills.

Beyond Dasheng, Zhang diversified into fisheries, salt production, an oil mill, and a flour mill, building an integrated regional industrial base centered on Nantong rather than a single-product company.
Resigned from a path toward further imperial office after placing first in the 1894 top-level civil service examination, and instead built the Dasheng Cotton Mill in Nantong starting in 1895.
Took an official post as Industrial and Commercial Secretary in Yuan Shikai's early Republican government in 1913, then resigned in 1915 to return to Nantong.
Zhang resigned his national government post in 1915 and returned to focus on Nantong's local industrial and education projects until his death in 1926.

The prospectus disclosed that the firm had reached operating profitability while scaling, a fact that distinguished it from the loss-on-listing profile of most Indian consumer-tech peers and that anchored the IPO's premium pricing.

The post-IPO pivot toward Nykaa Fashion and the eBZ retail-store buildout reflected a preference for owned channels over a marketplace extension, preserving margin control at the cost of slower scaling.

Zong grew up in poverty in Zhejiang, dropped out of middle school, was part of China's 'sent-down' youth movement, and worked at a salt farm in Zhoushan before eventually returning to Hangzhou and taking menial school-related work.

Zong built Wahaha from what began as a government-owned Hangzhou sales company founded in 1987 into China's largest beverage producer, leading it continuously as chairman, general manager, and later CEO.
Reneged on a December 2006 agreement to sell a majority stake in Wahaha's non-JV operations to Danone, triggering formal legal disputes in 2007.

Danone and Wahaha suspended their legal battle on December 21, 2007 and resumed negotiations; in 2009 Danone exited the joint venture entirely, selling its 51% stake back to Wahaha Group for an estimated $500 million.

Chen took Shanda's parent company private in early 2012, with himself, his wife Chrissy Luo, and his brother retaining a combined 57% stake, converting the group into a family-owned global investment company.

In late 2016, Chen and his wife created the Tianqiao and Chrissy Chen Institute, committing $1 billion to support fundamental brain-science research through partnerships with Caltech, Huashan Hospital, and Shanghai Mental Health Center.
Shanda became China's largest internet company by market capitalization in 2004, with three subsidiaries eventually listed on NASDAQ and one on KOSDAQ.
Shanda Group operates today as a family-owned global investment company under Chen's continued leadership as founder, chairman and CEO.
Committed $1 billion in late 2016 to found the Tianqiao and Chrissy Chen Institute for brain science research.
The Chen Institute established Chen Frontier Labs and has funded programs supporting young scientists and brain-focused conferences globally, per Shanda's own team page.

Chen earned an economics degree from Fudan University in 1993, worked at state-owned developer Shanghai Lujiazui Group and then Kinghing Trust & Investment, before starting online gaming company Shanda with family members in 1999.

Shanda became the largest internet company in China by market capitalization in 2004, and Chen was recognized that year on Hurun Report's rich list, CCTV's 'Rising Business Star,' and MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 list.
Built Evergrande into China's largest real-estate developer through aggressive, debt-financed expansion into real estate, sports, entertainment, and beverages.

Evergrande defaulted in 2021, failed to repay billions of dollars in wealth-management products, and was delisted from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on August 25, 2025, per AP's photo caption reporting.
Chinese authorities detained Xu in 2023 following the default; he was not seen in public again until his April 2026 trial, according to the Guardian.

China's securities regulator separately fined Xu $6.6 million in 2024 and imposed a lifetime securities-market ban after finding Evergrande had committed disclosure-related violations, according to the Guardian's April 2026 report.
Co-founded Mindray in Shenzhen in 1991 with Xu Hang and Cheng Minghe, focused on domestic patient-monitoring, imaging, and diagnostic products.
Listed Mindray on the NYSE in 2006, then took it private in a 2016 buyout led by Li and the other two co-founders, followed by a re-listing on China's A-share market.
Founded ICT New Technology Development Company (later Legend, then Lenovo) in 1984 using a state-institute investment.
Retired as Chairman of Legend Holdings in December 2019, handing the role to CFO Ning Min while retaining honorary chairman, senior adviser, and strategy-committee positions.

Ning Min succeeded Liu as Legend Holdings chairman in December 2019; Liu remained honorary chairman, senior adviser, and a member of the board's strategy committee, per SCMP's report on the exchange filing.
Returned to the Lenovo chairmanship in February 2009 during the global financial crisis to steer a turnaround.
Lenovo achieved a successful turnaround under Liu and Yang Yuanqing, regaining momentum in the PC market and expanding into mobile internet, per Lenovo's own 2011 press release.
Founded New Oriental and built it into China's largest private off-campus education services company prior to the 2021 regulatory crackdown.

Personally launched a live-streaming e-commerce career on Douyin in December 2021 and expanded it through 2022, pivoting the company toward selling agricultural and other goods, incorporating English-teaching content as a hook.

Fosun's December 2015 disclosure described Guo Guangchang as assisting authorities with an investigation, a characterization that accompanied his brief absence from public view before his return to the company four days later.
Founded and chaired Fosun Group from 1994, diversifying it into a large multi-sector conglomerate and listing its holding company, Fosun International, on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2007.

Fosun International grew into one of China's largest privately held conglomerates, with a market value reported at HK$157.4 billion (approximately US$20.17 billion) as of the November 2017 Reuters report.
Stepped down as chairman of subsidiary Shanghai Fosun High Technology (Group) in November 2017 to give younger executives more responsibility, while remaining chairman of parent Fosun International.

Guo remained chairman of Fosun International, continuing to focus on broader group strategy following his 2017 subsidiary-level resignation; as of Forbes' July 2024 estimate, his personal net worth was US$2.8 billion.
Zhang holds a bachelor's degree from Tsinghua University and a PhD from MIT, an academic background distinct from many domestic-trained internet-era Chinese founders.
Zhang founded Sohu, which listed on NASDAQ in 2000, and was ranked 37th on Forbes China's Richest list in 2000 and 20th in 2003, reflecting Sohu's early prominence among Chinese internet portals.

Sohu became one of China's earliest and best-known internet portals; Zhang has since taken on an adjunct professorship at HKUST and become a public commentator on career and education topics, per SCMP.

Co-founder Cheng Yixiao, who created the Kuaishou app a decade earlier as a tool for creating and sharing animated pictures, took over as CEO and became responsible for company operations, reporting structurally to Su as chairman.
Kuaishou had gone public in Hong Kong earlier in 2021 and had grown into China's second-largest short-video platform after ByteDance's Douyin, per SCMP.
Stepped down as Kuaishou CEO in October 2021, transferring operational responsibility to co-founder Cheng Yixiao while remaining chairman.
Su remained chairman of Kuaishou with unchanged voting rights, while Cheng Yixiao assumed CEO responsibilities for company operations.
Li founded and continues to lead NIO as chairman and CEO, a dual role he has held since the company's founding, per Wikipedia and LinkedIn.
NIO grew into a major Chinese EV maker, with Li remaining chairman and CEO and maintaining public visibility, including a 2026 return to his alma mater.
Rong Desheng entered employment at the Shanghai Tongshun Bank in 1890, then co-founded a small flour mill in Wuxi with his brother in 1902 using savings from their banking business.

During the Second Sino-Japanese War, after his brother's 1938 death, Rong Desheng took control of the business empire and, despite severe financial pressure and threats to his life, refused to sell the enterprise to Japanese interests.
In the chaotic aftermath of the war, Rong Desheng was kidnapped twice by gangsters reportedly backed by corrupt Kuomintang-linked officials seeking to extort money from him.
Assumed sole leadership of the family's flour-and-textile empire after his brother Rong Zongjing's death in 1938.
Refused Japanese demands to sell or cede control of the Rong enterprises despite financial pressure and personal threats.
The Rong enterprise survived the war under Chinese family control rather than being sold to Japanese interests, per Wikipedia's biography.
Chose to remain on the Chinese mainland and cooperate with the incoming Communist government after 1949 rather than emigrate with capital to Hong Kong or Taiwan.
Lai has been deeply involved in China's express-delivery industry for over 20 years and previously served as deputy chairman of the China Express Delivery Association.
Lai studied at 'Lakeside University' (Hupan University, an institution co-founded by Jack Ma) and at Tsinghua University's PBC School of Finance, per ZTO's own management biography.
Lai is a brother-in-law to fellow ZTO executive Jianchang Lai, per the company's own disclosed management biography, indicating a family relationship among top ZTO leadership.
Founded ZTO Express and has served as chairman since May 2013 and CEO since the company's inception.
Lai Meisong's ZTO Express my 2025 | Lai Meisong: High-Quality Development to Reduce Overall Logistics.
Lai Meisong's ZTO Express lai Meisong, founder, Chairman, and CEO of ZTO Express, the full year of 2018.
Wang founded BYD in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery maker before diversifying into automobiles and, later, electric vehicles.
Founded BYD in 1995 as a battery manufacturer, later expanding into automobiles and electric vehicles.
BYD grew into one of the world's largest electric-vehicle makers, with Wang publicly targeting global automaker leadership by scale within five years as of his June 2026 remarks.
Rose through Gree's sales and management ranks from 1990 saleswoman to president (2001) to chairwoman (2012).
Gree grew into a major conglomerate with annual revenue exceeding CNY 200 billion, and Dong became known as China's 'home appliances queen.'.
When Zhang took over as general manager of the Qingdao Refrigerator Plant (Haier's predecessor), it had annual sales of just 3.48 million yuan and a loss of 1.47 million yuan.
Soon after being appointed general manager, Zhang had 76 defective refrigerators smashed in front of staff to instill quality-control discipline among employees.

Zhang implemented strict, military-style workplace rules at Haier, including fines for employees who did not push in their chairs when leaving desks, reflecting an operating culture centered on discipline and process control.

Haier pursued an active foreign-acquisition strategy under Zhang, including acquiring New Zealand appliance maker Fisher & Paykel in 2012 and Sanyo's Japanese white-goods business around 2011, as part of global expansion.

Stepped down as Haier Group chairman and CEO in November 2021, with President Zhou Yunjie succeeding him as chairman and CEO; Zhang volunteered not to be renominated as a director and became honorary chairman.

Zhou Yunjie became chairman and CEO of Haier Group in November 2021, with Zhang remaining honorary chairman; the company subsequently continued to promote the 'Rendanheyi' management model Zhang had championed.
Zhou founded 3721 in 1998, a search engine that sold Chinese-language keywords for Roman-alphabet domain names, an early and distinctly China-specific internet business model.
China's operations, but differences between Zhou and Yahoo's management led Yahoo to sell its China operations to Alibaba in 2005, after which Zhou departed to start Qihoo 360.
As of November 2018, Forbes ranked Zhou #45 on its China Rich List and #135 on its global Billionaires list, with an estimated net worth of $4.7 billion.
Left Yahoo! China after management disagreements and founded Qihoo 360 following Yahoo's 2005 sale of its China operations to Alibaba.
Founded Pop Mart in 2010 and built its collectible blind-box toy business, including the Labubu and Skullpanda product lines.
Pop Mart's Labubu-driven growth made Wang China's 10th richest individual by June 2025, with a Forbes-estimated net worth of $19.6 billion as of February 2026.
Signaled a strategic pivot toward balanced, sustainable growth and category diversification (including home appliances) following the March 2026 share-price drop.

As of the March 25, 2026 report, the market reaction (a sharp share drop) had occurred, but the ultimate success of the balanced-growth and diversification strategy was not yet determinable from the source.

Co-founded the Hope Group with three siblings in 1982, starting with quail and chicken hatching, then agreed to split the group into four separate sibling-led companies in 1995, retaining and building East Hope Group.
East Hope Group grew into a major diversified enterprise spanning agribusiness, chemicals, and non-ferrous metals, with Liu Yongxing continuing as its founder, chairman and CEO.
Founded Li Auto and has continued serving as its chairman and CEO, prioritizing gross-margin discipline amid competitive pressure as of mid-2026.
Li Auto continued operating under Li's leadership as of mid-2026, with the company's margin-focused strategy's ultimate financial.
Founded SF Express in the early 1990s to provide express delivery between Guangdong manufacturers and Hong Kong buyers.

SF Express grew into SF Holding, a major Shenzhen-based multinational logistics conglomerate, with Wang remaining chairman and majority shareholder and an estimated net worth of $15.3 billion as of August 2026 per Wikipedia.

After leaving the military and working briefly for a Shenzhen oil-logistics company, Ren founded Huawei in September 1987 with registered capital of 21,000 yuan, reportedly out of dissatisfaction with his prior job.
Founded Huawei Technologies in Shenzhen in September 1987 as a private telecommunications equipment reseller/manufacturer.

Huawei grew into, per Wikipedia's characterization, the world's largest telecommunications equipment manufacturer and a top-tier global smartphone maker, with Ren remaining CEO nearly four decades later.

He is described by the Yidan Prize Foundation as the 'Father of Internet Philanthropy' and ranked top of the 13th China Charity Ranking in 2016 and as China's top philanthropist on the 2017 Forbes China Philanthropist list.
Co-founded Tencent in 1998 and served as Chief Administrative Officer, later launching the Tencent Charity Foundation in 2007.
Stepped down as Tencent CAO in March 2013 to dedicate himself full-time to philanthropy, founding the Chen Yidan Charity Foundation and later the Yidan Prize (2016).

Chen established Wuhan College, the Chen Yidan Charity Foundation, and the HK$2.5 billion Yidan Prize, and was recognized as China's top philanthropist in national rankings, while retaining honorary ties to Tencent's charity arm.
On June 10, 2026, He announced he would personally take charge of Xpeng's robot unit, with mass production of its humanoid robot 'Iron' described as imminent, per Reuters.
Took direct charge of Xpeng's robotics unit on June 10, 2026, ahead of imminent mass production of its humanoid robot.
As of the June 10, 2026 Reuters report, Xpeng's humanoid robot mass production was described as imminent under He's direct oversight; the actual production launch.
Founded Haidilao and grew it into a leading Chinese hot pot chain before stepping back in recent years to focus on high-level strategy as chairman.
Resumed the CEO role on January 13, 2026, to lead an accelerated strategic overhaul, including the 'Red Pomegranate Plan' to diversify beyond hot pot.
Founded Suntech Power in 2001 with Wuxi municipal government backing and led its rapid growth through a 2005 NYSE listing.
Suntech's 2005 listing made Shi briefly the richest person in China (peak net worth $2.9 billion in 2008) and triggered a wave of local-government investment in solar manufacturing across China.

Following his 2013 removal, Shi Zhengrong publicly characterized the board's action against him as procedurally flawed and lacking lawful basis, a disputed claim presented against the board's own account of the ouster.
Suntech accumulated $2.2 billion in debt and defaulted on a $541 million bond; five days after that default, its main operating subsidiary, Wuxi Suntech Power, filed for bankruptcy protection.
After Suntech's 2005 NYSE listing, Shi became the richest person in China, with a peak net worth of $2.9 billion in 2008 (ranking No.
396 on Forbes' World's Billionaires List);, his post-listing wealth created a demonstration effect that prompted local governments across China to invest heavily in the solar industry.
Before founding Baidu, Li worked as an engineer at Infoseek, an early search-industry pioneer, and as a senior consultant for IDD Information Services, per Baidu's own management biography.
Li has served as Baidu's chairman since the company's inception in January 2000 and added the CEO title in February 2004, after initially serving as president from 2000 to 2003.

Li holds a bachelor's degree in information science from Peking University and a master's in computer science from the State University of New York at Buffalo, and serves on the board of New Oriental Education & Technology Group.
Baidu became China's dominant search engine, with Li remaining chairman and CEO for over two decades, per the company's own investor-relations biography.
Ltd. over disputes tied to financing failures on a major Wanda development project in Wuhan; Caixin reported Wang's name was later removed from the public version of the order.
Wanda has been selling assets and renegotiating debt to manage a severe liquidity crisis, having raised billions of yuan in 2023 through such measures, per Caixin's reporting.
Pursued large-scale real estate and cultural-tourism development projects (including in Wuhan) financed substantially through trust and other debt instruments.
Failed repayment on the Wuhan project financing led Everbright Xinglong Trust to seek court intervention, resulting in high-consumption restrictions on Wang and Wanda entities as of September 2025.
Lei joined Kingsoft as an engineer in 1992, became its CEO in 1998, led it to a 2007 Hong Kong Stock Exchange IPO, then resigned as president and CEO on December 20, 2007, citing health reasons.
In 2000 Lei founded online retailer joyo.com, which he sold to Amazon.com for $75 million in 2004; in 2005 he made a $1 million investment in YY that was later worth far more after the company's IPO.
Resigned as president and CEO of Kingsoft on December 20, 2007, citing health reasons, after leading it to an IPO earlier that year.
Lei has driven Xiaomi's expansion beyond smartphones into electric vehicles and semiconductors, per SCMP's June 2025 characterization of him as 'transforming Xiaomi into a technology conglomerate.'.
Founded Xiaomi and later steered the company into new segments including electric vehicles and chips.
By May 2025, Forbes estimated Lei's net worth at $42.6 billion, ranking him 33rd worldwide, per Wikipedia's citation, reflecting Xiaomi's growth including its EV pivot.
Retained the 'honorary chairman' title at Kingsoft Office (WPS Office maker) as of June 2025, despite his primary focus on Xiaomi.

Cheng founded Didi in 2012, initially launching as taxi-hailing app Didi Dache, then merged with rival Kuaidi Dache in 2015 and acquired Uber's China operations in 2016 in exchange for an equity stake.
Didi delisted from the NYSE in June 2022 and, per Wikipedia, was permitted to resume new user registrations in China in early 2023 following regulatory review.
Founded Didi Dache in 2012 and pursued rapid growth via the 2015 Kuaidi Dache merger and 2016 Uber China acquisition.
Didi stated on Weibo that it fully accepted the regulator's decision and would rectify its wrongdoings.
Proceeded with a $4.4 billion NYSE IPO on June 30, 2021, days before Chinese regulators opened a cybersecurity investigation into the company.
Zhang was born April 1, 1983 in Longyan, Fujian, and studied microelectronics engineering at Nankai University in Tianjin before founding ByteDance in 2012.

Zhang announced in May 2021 that he would step down as CEO, completing the handover on November 4, 2021, while remaining chairman and retaining more than 50 percent of ByteDance's voting rights, per Reuters as cited by Wikipedia.
Bloomberg estimated Zhang's net worth at $92.8 billion as of June 2026, and Wikipedia states the global popularity of TikTok made him the richest man in China in 2024.
Stepped down as CEO of ByteDance on November 4, 2021, completing a handover announced in May 2021, while remaining chairman.

Pan Shiyi married his third wife, Zhang Xin, in 1994, and the couple co-founded SOHO China in 1995 in Beijing, building it from scratch into a major office-property developer during China's real estate boom.
Pan and Zhang converted to the Bahá'í Faith in 2005 and established the Soho China Foundation the same year to support underprivileged families through education initiatives.
Co-founded SOHO China with Zhang Xin in 1995, building it into a major Beijing-focused office developer.
Pursued a sale of the couple's controlling SOHO China stake to Blackstone Group starting in 2020, and after that deal fell through, resigned as chairman effective September 7, 2022.
Founded venture capital firm Innovation Works in 2009, later renamed Sinovation Ventures, investing in AI startups.
Founded 01.AI in 2023, a Beijing-based AI company building agentic tools for companies worldwide using customized open-source models.
